project_notice: This guide does not replace official evacuation orders or emergency services. It cannot predict disasters and shows no live alerts.

before.text: Make a home escape plan with a meeting place outside. Know two ways out of every room, practise them, and practise feeling your way out with your eyes closed.
before.caveat: Partly sourced from Delhi Fire Service (Delhi Govt) pages, which are Delhi Government guidance, not nationwide rules.

before.text: Keep exit routes and staircases clear, and check them periodically.
before.caveat: Partly sourced from Delhi Fire Service (Delhi Govt) pages, which are Delhi Government guidance, not nationwide rules.

before.text: Know how to operate the fire alarm and the firefighting equipment.
before.caveat: Delhi Government guidance (Delhi Fire Service), not a nationwide rule.

before.text: Fit working smoke alarms.
Keep extinguishers (refilled), buckets of water and blankets ready.
Get a fire audit, and keep combustibles away from loose wiring.
Keep hydrants and access to firefighting equipment clear, and do not tamper with the equipment.
before.caveat: Delhi Government guidance (Delhi Fire Service), not a nationwide rule.

during.text: A small flame can become a major fire in under 30 seconds. Smoke and toxic gases kill more people than flames, and there is only time to escape.
during.caveat: Delhi Government guidance (Delhi Fire Service), not a nationwide rule.

during.text: Exit immediately if the fire is out of control.
Never go back for possessions.
during.caveat: Partly sourced from Delhi Fire Service (Delhi Govt) pages, which are Delhi Government guidance, not nationwide rules.

during.text: Leave by the nearest exit.
during.caveat: Partly sourced from Delhi Fire Service (Delhi Govt) pages, which are Delhi Government guidance, not nationwide rules.

during.text: Escape first, then call for help.
during.caveat: Delhi Government guidance (Delhi Fire Service), not a nationwide rule.

during.text: Do not use lifts, and do not shout or run.
during.caveat: Partly sourced from Delhi Fire Service (Delhi Govt) pages, which are Delhi Government guidance, not nationwide rules.

during.text: Close doors and windows behind you, and do not prop fire or smoke-check doors open.
during.caveat: Partly sourced from Delhi Fire Service (Delhi Govt) pages, which are Delhi Government guidance, not nationwide rules.

during.text: Once you are out, raise the alarm and call 112.
during.caveat: Partly sourced from Delhi Fire Service (Delhi Govt) pages, which are Delhi Government guidance, not nationwide rules.

during.text: Attempt to put out a fire only if you can do so without undue risk.
during.caveat: This combined wording was explicitly approved by the project owner. Partly sourced from Delhi Fire Service (Delhi Govt) pages, which are Delhi Government guidance, not nationwide rules.

during.text: Check a closed door with the back of your hand at the top, the knob and the frame.
during.caveat: No source tag is given for this lead-in line in the Stage 2 content; it introduces the two closed-door items that follow.

during.text: Closed door: if it is hot, do not open it, and use another exit.
during.caveat: Partly sourced from Delhi Fire Service (Delhi Govt) pages, which are Delhi Government guidance, not nationwide rules.

during.text: Closed door: if it is cool, open it slowly while bracing your shoulder against it. If heat or smoke comes in, slam it shut and use your alternate route.
during.caveat: Delhi Government guidance (Delhi Fire Service), not a nationwide rule.

during.text: Stay low and crawl under smoke.
during.caveat: Partly sourced from Delhi Fire Service (Delhi Govt) pages, which are Delhi Government guidance, not nationwide rules.

during.text: If you cannot get out: stay close to the floor if smoke permeates.
If you cannot get out: if you cannot use a door, use a window. If it is too high to jump, attract attention by waving something.
If you cannot get out: keep doors closed and block gaps with a wet cloth to slow the spread of smoke.
during.caveat: Mandatory owner-approved clarification: The wet cloth at the door gap only aims to slow smoke entering. It does not filter smoke and does not make the room safe. Do not imply that this action protects people from toxic smoke. Calling 112 and seeking rescue must not be delayed.

during.text: If you cannot get out: call 112.
If someone is missing, tell the firefighters.
during.caveat: Delhi Government guidance (Delhi Fire Service), not a nationwide rule.

during.text: If your clothes catch fire: stop, drop to the ground and roll to put out the flames.
If someone else is burning: put out the flames by dousing with water or wrapping them in a blanket. Remove the blanket as soon as the flames are out.
If someone else is burning: if electricity is involved, switch off the main supply.
Help firefighters: give way to fire engines.
during.caveat: Partly sourced from Delhi Fire Service (Delhi Govt) pages, which are Delhi Government guidance, not nationwide rules.

during.text: Help firefighters: guide them to water sources.
during.caveat: Partly sourced from Delhi Fire Service (Delhi Govt) pages, which are Delhi Government guidance, not nationwide rules.

during.text: Help firefighters: do not park near hydrants or water tanks.
during.caveat: Partly sourced from Delhi Fire Service (Delhi Govt) pages, which are Delhi Government guidance, not nationwide rules.

during.text: Help firefighters: allow them to use your phone.
during.caveat: Delhi Government guidance (Delhi Fire Service), not a nationwide rule.

during.text: Help firefighters: keep the site uncrowded.
during.caveat: Delhi Government guidance (Delhi Fire Service), not a nationwide rule.

after.text: Burn first aid: cool the burned body part under running water, or immerse it in a bucket of water, for 10–15 minutes or until the burning pain subsides.
after.caveat: S1 and S7 · Delhi Govt say water until the pain subsides.

after.text: Burn first aid: do not immerse the whole body, and do not use ice or ice-cold water.
Burn first aid: cover the burn with a clean cloth and get to the nearest medical centre.
Burn first aid: do not apply any local agent to the wound.
Burn first aid: do not apply grease, ointment, lotion, antiseptic or ice, and do not break blisters.
Burn first aid: do not remove burnt clothing unless it comes off easily, and do not try to remove anything melted into the skin.
Burn first aid: do not apply adhesive dressing.
Burns suffered in a closed space can cause carbon monoxide poisoning and need prompt medical care.
Get urgent medical help for someone with burns to the face, singed nasal hair, soot in the sputum, hoarseness, cough or difficulty breathing.

subsections.description: Subsection of Fire, not a separate disaster category. The Preparation items apply if you live in or near forest.

prevention.text: Never leave a fire unattended near forest. Douse it with water and stir the ashes until cold.
Be careful with lanterns, stoves and heaters when camping. Cool them before refuelling, avoid spills, and store fuel away from appliances.
Do not discard cigarettes or matches near forest, and do not leave a lit cigarette in dry vegetation.
Do not leave campfires or cigarettes unattended.
Do not burn stubble, municipal waste or dry farm waste next to forest.

preparation.text: Keep the contacts of the district fire service and local forest authorities handy.
Know your evacuation routes, keep supplies ready, practise drills and set safe meeting places.
Stay updated through local announcements, radio or alerts.
If told to leave, evacuation comes first.
Before leaving, if there is time: remove combustibles (firewood, yard waste, gas cylinders and fuel cans) from the yard.
Before leaving, if there is time: close windows, vents and doors, and close shutters or blinds.
Before leaving, if there is time: fill large vessels with water.
Before leaving, if there is time: cut back bushes close to the house, and clear leaves from roof and gutters.
Before leaving, if there is time: dampen the roof, walls and adjacent trees with water.
Wear protective clothing: cotton or woollen, sturdy shoes and a head covering.

emergency_evacuation.text: Evacuate immediately when instructed, and do not wait.
Take precautions against flying sparks and ashes, and untie cattle.
Help children, the elderly and disabled people to evacuate.
Report the fire immediately to forest officials, police or the fire service. In an emergency call 112.
Do not try to fight a large fire on your own.
If trapped, do not run uphill directly. Move sideways or downhill. Fires spread faster uphill.
If a closed door at home is hot, do not open it.
Do not drive through heavy smoke. If you cannot see ahead, do not risk it.
Do not block emergency vehicle routes, and do not spread rumours.
Do not enter the forest during a fire.

after.text: Do not return until authorities declare it safe.
NDRF lists unstable trees, ash pits and toxic fumes as hazards after a fire.
after.caveat: This source wording is written for firefighters.

common_preparedness.text: Plan ahead. Find out which disasters could affect your area, how to prepare, how you would be warned, and where evacuation routes and secure places are. Find safe spots in your home for each disaster.

Family plan. Keep these handy for each member: out-of-state contact, local contact, nearest relative, emergency phone number, family doctor and meeting places. Decide two meeting places: one near home for fire, and one outside the neighbourhood in case you cannot return. Keep emergency numbers near phones. Decide where to stay if told to evacuate, and learn shelter locations. Discuss power outages and injuries. Know national and local helplines. Keep a family member informed if you are caught in a disaster.

Escape plan. Draw your home marking doors, windows, steps, large furniture, emergency supplies, extinguishers, smoke detectors, first-aid kits and main utility connections. Show at least two escape routes from each room, plus a meeting place outside. Plan each floor separately. Practise evacuation at least twice a year.
common_preparedness.caveat: Credited to redcross.org in the source.

common_preparedness.text: Utilities. Show family members how to turn off the water, gas and electricity mains.

Emergency bag (waterproof). Sealed drinking water and dry non-perishable food, for example biscuits. Battery torch with spare batteries, and a battery radio. Candles and matches/lighter in a waterproof container. First-aid box, essential and prescription medicines, face mask, hand sanitiser and chlorine tablets. Knife, scissors, whistle, duct tape, paper and pencils, thick ropes and cords. Phone, charger and power bank. First-aid reference (book or photocopy). Emergency plan, local map, contact numbers and family details. Important documents, extra cash/valuables, spare vehicle and house keys, glasses or other personal aids. Soap, sanitary pads, wipes, toilet paper and paper towels. Weather-appropriate dry clothes including undergarments, blankets and protective footwear.

When warnings are issued. Store at least 5 litres of water per day for each person and each pet. Keep at least a three-day supply of water and food. Choose long-life foods needing little or no cooking, water or refrigeration, and avoid very salty or spicy items. Cater for babies and special diets. Keep the phone charged and use SMS. Store Aadhaar, ration card, voter ID and health/vaccination records in a waterproof bag. Follow authentic sources (mausam.imd.gov.in and ndma.gov.in).
common_preparedness.caveat: Conflict: S1 says a week of food and water for floods and cyclones. S4 says three days. The sources are not reconciled, so both recommendations must remain visible on those pages.

common_preparedness.text: First aid. Keep a first-aid box and learn basic first aid and CPR.
common_preparedness.caveat: Detailed first-aid steps are unavailable because NDMA's First Aid page could not be read.

common_preparedness.text: Children. Teach children how and when to call the national emergency number, 112.
common_preparedness.caveat: S4 lists 100/101/102/112; only 112 is shown here.

limitations.text: Items tagged Delhi Govt come from Delhi Fire Service pages. They are Delhi Government guidance, not nationwide rules.
Gap: no verified Indian official guidance on re-entering a burned building, structural or utility checks, cleanup, recovery or insurance. The Delhi Fire Service pages do not provide it.
Gap (Forest Fire): no other post-fire guidance for the public is verified.
Tamil Nadu Forest Department public survival guidance was not found on its official site.
Emergency number 112 is sourced to S4, X3† and X4†; X3† and X4† are excerpt-only evidence. Other state numbers are not displayed because their current status is unverified.
Detailed first-aid steps are unavailable because NDMA's First Aid page could not be read. First aid is limited to keeping a kit and learning first aid and CPR.
Recovery guidance is thin for every hazard.
NDMA's site pages, SACHET guidance files, the INCOIS User Guide, DG Fire Services PDFs and the TN Forest Department PDF were blocked to automated reading.
Source verification dates are not recorded per source. The research handover recorded access dates of 10 November 2026, but that date is not assigned to individual sources or claims.
